title: We’re opening a small beta for our AI-native browser game platform this Friday — would love feedback from AI game devs
author: Neon_Senpai
selftext:
Hi everyone, we’re opening a small beta this Friday for **Elseland**, an AI-native browser game platform we’ve been building around a simple idea: people should be able to create small playable games or worlds with AI, play them instantly in the browser, and remix or improve them without needing a full dev setup.

One thing we’re trying to be careful about is that the AI shouldn’t become “the whole game.” A lot of AI game demos are interesting for the first few minutes, but then the user is mostly watching things get generated instead of actually playing. We want the AI to help with creation, iteration, and remixing, while the game still has real choices, goals, and reasons to come back.

That’s the main thing we want to test in this beta: does the AI actually make game creation and remixing easier, or does it just feel like a cool generator? And after something is created, does it feel playable enough for people to stay, share, or improve it?

I’d really appreciate thoughts from people here because this community probably understands the problem better than most. For AI-assisted games, what do you think makes the difference between a “cool demo” and something people actually want to play?

We’re gathering a small group of early testers for Friday. Happy to share the beta invite if anyone wants to try it and give feedback.
